items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: So I get the call from Count Basie... we want you to join the band starting October 8... I was 24 years old... My rehearsal was in the dressing room with Basie

ctx.x: Yeah the guys called him a various assortment of names. Bill, Chief. I called him Chief. Some guys called him Count. Other guys called him Boss. It didn’t matter, he was just so well respected. He was a great guy. So I get the call from Count Basie. So he said, “Sonny Cohn, the manager, will be calling you shortly and he’ll let you know all the details.” He said, “we want you to join the band starting October 8.” And that was Labor Day. So that’s like six weeks. I was registered for school, all ready to go back…

what have I gotten myself into. After the first song we played the first night, I’ll never forget, Toledo, Ohio, Masonic Auditorium, 2000 people in the audience. And we played “Wind Machine” the first song. It was always the first opener. Sammy Nestico’s. Like a bat out of hell. And when we got to the end of that, the very first song I played with the band was “Wind Machine.” I was shaking so badly physically. I was behind the drums going I can’t believe this is it. Of course the next tune was a blues, and Basie…
